results.title: Chickpea Production
results.description: Growth habit Chickpea develops a taproot and lateral roots to a depth of about 30 inches. The plant has an indeterminate growth habit which allows plants to develop new leaves after flowering has begun. Typically, chickpea growth and development is terminated by some form of environmental stress, such as drought or extreme heat. Late season rains can cause plants that appear to have gone dormant to resume development including flowering and seed set, complicating harvest management. Chemical [...] Climate Chickpea is a cool season crop that grows best when daytime temperatures are between 70 and 84 °F, and nighttime temperatures are between 64 and 70 °F. The crop does well in regions with 6-10 inches of growing season precipitation. Temperatures above 98 °F can cause stress during early flowering and pod development, resulting in reduced yields. But chickpea performs better than dry pea and lentil under heat and drought stress. Chickpea as a crop is somewhat drought tolerant. Cultural [...] the growth habit of chickpea is more upright than peas or lentils and seeds are set higher on the plant.    •Vegetative-stage deficits caused < 7% yield reduction. 
   •Peak water productivity occurred at 519–538 mm irrigation. 
   •Elevated VPD and wind reduced yields by ∼30%.
